mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during tightening cycles (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% in a month indicates a tightening labor market, which increases wage costs and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of tightening labor markets (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP by more than 2% over a quarter signals strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of strong GDP growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of increased industrial production (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts by more than 10% in a month signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which reduces economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of decreased housing starts (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index by more than 0.5% in a month signals inflationary pressure, which increases costs and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of increased inflation (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in nonfarm payrolls and a decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.2% in a month signals a strengthening labor market, which increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases & UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of joint labor market improvement (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real retail and food services sales by more than 1% over a quarter signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of increased retail and food services sales (t-test p > 0.05).
